shortName: University of Colorado School of Medicine
additionalCoursework:
CUSOM does not require or recommend premedical coursework. CUSOM recognizes that the experiences and undergraduate academic experience of our applicants varies greatly. We encourage applicants to explore a diverse, interdisciplinary, and balanced undergraduate education, encompassing the necessary foundational knowledge in the biomedical sciences and humanities. Students need to be adequately prepared in the scientific underpinnings of modern medicine and understand the psychosocial elements that are critical to its practice. 

Competitive applicants should demonstrate in-depth competency in each of the following areas of study, as reflected by their academic achievements and letters of recommendation:

Biology, Chemistry/Biochemistry, Mathematics/Statistics and Physics, Social Sciences and Communication

Students are encouraged to consider additional coursework in biochemistry, computer sciences, genetics, humanities, and social sciences.

medSchoolStudLife.diversity: We believe diversity enhances the learning environment, strengthens the visibility and ties to nearby communities, and contributes to the community’s overall health through programs and trainings focused on decreasing health disparities and increasing health equity. The university supports diversity of its student body through increased community outreach, pipeline programs, student groups, and financial support.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Leave of Absence requests are handled by the Student Promotions Committee.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: There are many active student organizations, ranging from career specialty interest groups, to student government to community based organizations. There are also tracks available as non-required components of the curriculum.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: CUSOM is an urban campus in Aurora, Colorado. In addition to the schools on the campus, the University of Colorado Hospital, The Children's Hospital, the Veteran Affairs Medical Center, the Barbara Davis Center for Childhood Diabetes, and the Ben Nighthorse Campbell Center for Native American Studies are on the CU Anschutz Campus.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Rental property and roommate information are available in the Student Assistance Office. Call 303-724-7684 or visit https://www.cuanschutz.edu/student/resources/housing
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: The school's mission is to support all students and help with creating a sense of belonging and inclusion, and to build community within the medical campus and beyond. There are multiple resources for student support across campus.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: CU Anschutz's Office of Disability, Access, & Inclusion (ODAI) recognizes, welcomes, and celebrates disability as an integral part of a diverse health professions campus and workforce.  ODAI provides accommodations and collaborates across campus partners on accessibility issues to support our growing and diverse disabled student population.   Learn more by visiting https://www.cuanschutz.edu/offices/office-of-disability-access-and-inclusion/students
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: Multiple school and campus-wide resources. Initial point of contact is the Office of Student Life within CUSOM.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: CU Anschutz is a vibrant, multidisciplinary health sciences campus dedicated to clinical care, education, and research. In addition to the school of medicine, other schools on campus include nursing, dentistry, physical therapy, physician assistant, public health, and pharmacy, to name a few.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo:
Educational and clinical activities during medical school require placement at various clinical sites throughout Colorado. Private reliable transportation is essential.
 
*Note: Accommodations to this policy can be requested through the Office of Disability, Access, and Inclusion and student preferences and specific limitations on travel distance will be considered.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Faculty may request professional attire for lectures or small group sessions that include patients or standardized patients. Professional attire is expected in the clinical setting.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Staff and faculty are available in the Office of Student Life to assist students.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Patient interaction begins early in first year through clinical skills training and preceptorship, and continues throughout in longitudinally integrated clerkships, electives, and acting internships.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Lecture, problem and team-based learning (small groups), observed clinical encounters, interactive/experiential, simulation
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Longitudinal integrated clerkships in which students participate in comprehensive care of patients over time and engage in continuity relationships with clinical faculty.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Learning medicine is best when working in teams and the first-year curriculum is designed to be interactive, experiential, and collaborative. Thus, students should be prepared to attend classes daily.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: CUSOM offers an innovative curriculum focusing on the pillars of Leadership, Curiosity and Commitment. Our curriculum integrates basic science longitudinally throughout all years to provide personal and professional development as clinicians and scientists. Curriculum is delivered phases: the Plains, the Foothills, the Alpine Ascent, and the Summit. The Plains is comprised of foundational experiences that take students through pre-clerkship integrated basic science curricula, clinical skills training, preceptorship and coaching. After a summer discovery period, students transition to the Foothills where they will participate in Longitudinal Integrated Clerkships (LICs). In the Alpine Ascent portion, students work through advanced science courses and USMLE. Students then find more individualized paths which include electives, dedicated research and discovery, acting internships, and critical care experiences. The Summit includes residency preparation and the match process.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: CUSOM has a commitment to primary care that is demonstrated through its clinical and research opportunities, electives, and community partnerships.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: A research track emphasizes traditional research opportunities with a focus on scientific discovery. Work will involve primarily lab-based bench-top research and/or computer simulations. The approach will be hypothesis-driven, with expectations for academic productivity  that includes dissemination of research work through peer-reviewed outlets, and the ability to formulate and defend research approaches. This track is most applicable to students interested in pursuing research careers in academia or industry. Research opportunities under this track are located at CU Anschutz and on other campuses in the University of Colorado system.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Some electives include a community service component.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: The Mentored Scholarly Activity is required for graduation.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: Denver Health Medical Center, National Jewish Hospital, Children's Hospital Colorado, University of Colorado Hospital, Veteran's Administration Hospital, and multiple other sites throughout Colorado.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: The University of Colorado School of Medicine (CUSOM) is a part of the University of Colorado located in Denver and Aurora, Colorado. The 230-acre CU Anschutz Campus in Aurora includes the Schools of Dentistry, Nursing, Pharmacy, Public Health, and the Graduate School as well as CUSOM. Clinical opportunities for medical students are located throughout the Denver metropolitan area and Colorado. CUSOM is home to > 5,000 full-time and approximately 3,000 community volunteer faculty. Student research opportunities and a variety of extracurricular activities are available.
medSchoolInformation.programAbout: The BA/BS-MD degree program at the University of Colorado Denver (CU Denver) | CU Anschutz is designed to address Colorado’s health care needs by selecting up to ten exceptional students each year who are dedicated to serving the health care needs of the state. The program is a partnership between the University of Colorado Denver College of Liberal Arts and Sciences and the University of Colorado School of Medicine.

medSchoolApplication.cbcRequired: Criminal background checks are required for all accepted students who matriculate to CUSOM. Background checks are not used at any point in the selection process.
medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: Committee letters fulfill the minimum requirement.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: CUSOM prefers letters from those that have a longitudinal relationship with the applicant and speak specifically to the applicant's competencies expected of entering medical students.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Structured interviews with group and individual interviews, virtual.
medSchoolApplication.secApplSentTo: Applicants with MCAT equal to or greater than 500
medSchoolApplication.stateResAfterMatric: Yes, but accountable student fee still applies.
medSchoolApplication.acceptOutstateApplInformation: CUSOM accepts out of state applicants.
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
Secondary applications are requested from selected candidates. We do not send secondary applications to all applicants. Once the secondary application is completed and the $100 secondary application fee is paid (waived for FAP applicants), files are reviewed for consideration for interview. 

 Students are interviewed on Wednesdays and Fridays. Interviews begin in August and conclude in February. Our admissions committee uses holistic review to account for an applicant's experiences, attributes, and metrics to make an admissions decision.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo: A highest total MCAT score on a single test of 500 or greater is required to receive a secondary application.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: No minimum undergraduate GPA for consideration of other coursework
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: No minimum number of credit hours for consideration of other coursework
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: Coursework completed at a community college is reviewed in the context of the applicant's entire educational journey.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: CUSOM participates in federal aid programs and has a number of merit- and need-based scholarships. Colorado student grant funds are available for Colorado residents. Financial aid questions should be directed to 303-724-8039.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec: CUSOM requires that students have a baccalaureate degree from, or have completed 120 semester hours, across a 4-year curriculum at an accredited college or university by the time of matriculation. We recognize that the experiences and undergraduate academic experience of our applicants varies greatly. We encourage applicants to explore a diverse, interdisciplinary and balanced undergraduate education, encompassing the necessary foundational knowledge in the biomedical sciences and humanities. Students need to be adequately prepared in the scientific underpinnings of modern medicine and also understand the psychosocial elements that are critical to its practice. Accordingly, we have moved away from traditional, specific course based requirements, and have revised our prerequisites and academic expectations such that students should provide evidence to demonstrate competencies in the life sciences, social sciences, physics and mathematics.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: Class seats are offered to the applicants who are most highly qualified in terms of intelligence, achievement, character, motivation, and maturity. Grades, MCAT scores, recommendations, and personal interviews are assessed. A holistic review process also values aptitudes and experience. Humanistic qualities, indications of peer collaboration, and professionalism are characteristics of our students. Applicants from rural areas and from groups underrepresented in medicine are encouraged to apply. All undergraduate majors are considered acceptable. Excellent performance in science courses is essential. The medical school has an active Medical Scientist Training Program (MSTP) for those who wish to combine medical school with intensive laboratory research. CUSOM does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, pregnancy, sex, age, disability, creed, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, veteran status, or political affiliation.
